topic.title: Getting Started with Translation
topic.shortdesc: A hands-on walkthrough of the translation workflow using the Hydraulic Gear Pump sample project.

body.p: The steps below walk you through the complete translation workflow, from editing English content to publishing a multilingual deliverable.

li.p: Create a project from the Hydraulic Gear Pump sample - Create a new project and choose the Hydraulic Gear Pump sample template. See Projects for the full procedure. Take a moment to explore the project:

ul.li: It is already set up with an en/ folder for the English source and a separate folder for each translation, as described in Choosing a Project Structure for Translation.
It includes a translation index that shows the current state of the project.

It includes a multilingual DITA map that contains all DITA maps for the individual languages in separate key scopes, a publication named Gear Pump Multilingual, and a PDF deliverable associated with it.

li.p: Make a change to one of the topics - Open one of the English topics in the visual editor and make a small change, such as adding a new step. See Reviewing and Editing Files in the Visual Editor. Then commit the change.

Run the translation for all supported languages - Start a new translation job. In the New translation dialog box, choose the Publication to translate and one or more Target Language values. Optionally, add free-form Translation Instructions for the agent, then select Start translation. A single job covers all the languages that you selected and translates them one after another, so prefer one job over several parallel ones. See Running an Incremental Translation for details about what happens while the job runs.

Monitor the job and bring in the results - Each job appears as a card that shows its progress. You can stop a running job from its card. When a job finishes, select Bring into workspace on the card to add the translated files to your workspace.
Review and commit the translated files - Review the translated files and the translation index that were added to your workspace, then commit them. See Reviewing Translations Before You Commit.

Publish the multilingual PDF - Open the project's Deliverables page and build the Gear Pump to Multilingual PDF deliverable. This publishes the translated languages together with the English source in a single PDF.

body.p: Repeat the edit-translate-publish cycle as often as needed. Because tracks translation state incrementally, later jobs retranslate only the topics that you changed.

p.note: also provides a template project that you can use as a starting point for your own translated content. It is set up in the same way as this sample, with a multilingual book deliverable and DITA keys defined for each language. See Projects for information about creating a project from a template.
